title_en: Provisions of the Supreme People's Court, Supreme People's Procuratorate, Ministry of Public Security, Ministry of State Security, Ministry of Justice, and the Legislative Affairs Commission of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress on Certain Issues Concerning the Implementation of the Criminal Procedure Law
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court, Supreme People's Procuratorate, Ministry of Public Security, Ministry of State Security, Ministry of Justice, Legislative Affairs Commission of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress

Regulations on Several Issues Concerning the Implementation of the Criminal Procedure Law

I. Jurisdiction

1. In accordance with the provisions of the Criminal Procedure Law on the division of jurisdiction over criminal cases, the People's Procuratorate has jurisdiction over "crimes of embezzlement and bribery, crimes of dereliction of duty by state functionaries, and crimes committed by state functionaries by taking advantage of their functions and powers such as illegal detention, extortion of confessions by torture, retaliation and false charges, illegal search, which infringe upon citizens' personal rights, and crimes infringing upon citizens' democratic rights." Cases involving tax-related and other matters shall be under the jurisdiction of the public security organs, which shall file and investigate the cases, and the People's Procuratorate shall no longer accept them. Any documents that do not conform to the provisions of the Criminal Procedure Law on the division of case jurisdiction shall be invalid.

For cases involving tax-related and other matters that are under the jurisdiction of the public security organs according to law but have already been filed and investigated by the People's Procuratorate, the People's Procuratorate may continue to handle them to completion, or the People's Procuratorate may transfer them to the public security organs for handling.

2. The Criminal Procedure Law provides that the People's Procuratorate has jurisdiction over cases of "crimes of dereliction of duty by state functionaries." The revised Criminal Law has amended the subject of dereliction of duty crimes to state functionaries. In accordance with this amendment, the "crimes of dereliction of duty" under the jurisdiction of the People's Procuratorate refer to the crimes of dereliction of duty stipulated in Chapter IX of the Specific Provisions of the Criminal Law. In addition, the crime of custodial personnel beating, physically punishing, or maltreating persons under custody as stipulated in Article 248 of Chapter IV of the Specific Provisions of the Criminal Law shall be under the jurisdiction of the People's Procuratorate. Crimes stipulated in Chapter III of the Specific Provisions of the Criminal Law on Crimes of Disrupting the Order of the Socialist Market Economy shall be under the jurisdiction of the public security organs.

3. The revised Criminal Law has explicitly stipulated the crimes of embezzlement and bribery in Chapter VIII of the Specific Provisions. In accordance with this amendment, the cases of "crimes of embezzlement and bribery" under the jurisdiction of the People's Procuratorate refer to the crimes of embezzlement and bribery stipulated in Chapter VIII of the Specific Provisions of the revised Criminal Law and the crimes in other chapters that are explicitly provided to be convicted and punished in accordance with the provisions on crimes of embezzlement and bribery in Chapter VIII of the Specific Provisions of the Criminal Law. The crimes stipulated in Paragraphs 1 and 2 of Article 163, Paragraph 1 of Article 184, and Article 164 shall be under the jurisdiction of the public security organs.

4. The "minor criminal cases with evidence provided by the victim" that are to be directly accepted by the People's Court as stipulated in Item 2 of Article 170 of the Criminal Procedure Law refer to the following criminal cases with evidence provided by the victim:

(1) Cases of intentional infliction of injury (minor injury);
(2) Cases of bigamy;
(3) Cases of abandonment;
(4) Cases of obstructing freedom of correspondence;
(5) Cases of illegally intruding into another person's residence;
(6) Cases of producing and selling fake or substandard goods (except those that seriously endanger social order and national interests);
(7) Cases of infringing upon intellectual property rights (except those that seriously endanger social order and national interests);
(8) Other minor criminal cases stipulated in Chapters IV and V of the Specific Provisions of the Criminal Law for which the defendant may be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not more than three years.

Among the eight categories of cases listed above, if the victim directly files a lawsuit with the People's Court, the People's Court shall accept it according to law. For those cases where the evidence is insufficient and may be accepted by the public security organs, they shall be transferred to the public security organs for filing and investigation. If the victim reports the case to the public security organs, the public security organs shall accept it.

Cases of perjury and refusal to execute judgments or orders shall be filed and investigated by the public security organs.

5. The revised Criminal Procedure Law has deleted the previous content that "the higher People's Court may, when necessary, assign a criminal case of first instance under its jurisdiction to a lower People's Court for trial." In accordance with this amendment, for criminal cases of first instance that are under the jurisdiction of a higher People's Court according to law, they may no longer be designated to a lower People's Court for jurisdiction.

6. When public security organs investigate criminal cases that involve cases of embezzlement and bribery under the jurisdiction of the People's Procuratorate, they shall transfer the cases of embezzlement and bribery to the People's Procuratorate; when the People's Procuratorate investigates cases of embezzlement and bribery that involve criminal cases under the jurisdiction of the public security organs, it shall transfer the criminal cases under the jurisdiction of the public security organs to the public security organs. In the above circumstances, if the suspected principal crime is under the jurisdiction of the public security organs, the public security organs shall take the lead in the investigation, with the cooperation of the People's Procuratorate; if the suspected principal crime is under the jurisdiction of the People's Procuratorate, the People's Procuratorate shall take the lead in the investigation, with the cooperation of the public security organs.

II. Case Filing

7. Article 87 of the Criminal Procedure Law stipulates: "If the People's Procuratorate considers that a public security organ should file a case for investigation but fails to do so, or if a victim considers that a public security organ should file a case for investigation but fails to do so and raises the matter with the People's Procuratorate, the People's Procuratorate shall demand that the public security organ provide an explanation for not filing the case. If the People's Procuratorate considers that the reasons given by the public security organ for not filing the case are untenable, it shall notify the public security organ to file the case, and the public security organ shall file the case upon receiving the notice." In accordance with the above provisions, within seven days after receiving the "Notice Requiring an Explanation for Not Filing the Case" from the People's Procuratorate, the public security organ shall provide a written explanation to the People's Procuratorate. When the People's Procuratorate considers that the reasons for not filing the case given by the public security organ are untenable and issues the "Notice to File the Case," it shall simultaneously transfer to the public security organ the relevant materials proving that the case should be filed. After receiving the "Notice to File the Case," the public security organ shall decide to file the case within fifteen days and deliver the decision to file the case to the People's Procuratorate.

III. Withdrawal

8. Articles 30 and 31 of the Criminal Procedure Law stipulate that the withdrawal of court clerks, interpreters, and expert witnesses shall be decided by the president of the People's Court. In accordance with this provision, the withdrawal of the above-mentioned personnel cannot be decided by the presiding judge.

IV. Participation of Lawyers in Criminal Proceedings

9. The "cases involving state secrets" as referred to in Article 96 of the Criminal Procedure Law mean cases where the facts or nature of the case involve state secrets. Cases shall not be considered as involving state secrets simply because relevant materials and handling opinions during the criminal investigation process need to be kept confidential.

10. In accordance with Article 96 of the Criminal Procedure Law, during the investigation stage, a criminal suspect may retain a lawyer by himself, or his relatives may retain one on his behalf. If a criminal suspect in custody requests to retain a lawyer, the custodial authority shall promptly convey the request to the relevant investigating authority handling the case, and the investigating authority shall promptly convey the request to the person entrusted by the suspect or the law firm to which that person belongs. If the criminal suspect only expresses the desire to retain a lawyer but does not specify a particular person, the investigating authority shall promptly notify the local lawyers association or judicial administrative authority to recommend a lawyer for him.

11. Article 96 of the Criminal Procedure Law stipulates that for cases involving state secrets, a lawyer's meeting with the criminal suspect in custody shall be subject to approval by the investigating authority. For cases not involving state secrets, a lawyer's meeting with the criminal suspect does not require approval. Cases shall not be deemed as involving state secrets and approval denied on the grounds that the investigation process needs to be kept confidential. When a lawyer requests to meet with the criminal suspect, the meeting shall be arranged within forty-eight hours. For major and complex joint crimes involving two or more persons, such as the crimes of organizing, leading, or participating in an organization of the nature of a criminal syndicate, organizing, leading, or participating in a terrorist organization, or crimes of smuggling, drug-related crimes, crimes of embezzlement and bribery, etc., when a lawyer requests to meet with the criminal suspect, the meeting shall be arranged within five days.

12. Article 96 of the Criminal Procedure Law stipulates that during the investigation stage, when a lawyer meets with a criminal suspect in custody, the investigating authority may, depending on the circumstances and needs of the case, send personnel to be present. During the stage of review for prosecution and the trial stage, when the investigation has been concluded and the defense lawyer or other defenders meet with the criminal suspect or defendant in custody, the People's Procuratorate and the People's Court shall not send personnel to be present.

13. During the trial stage, the defense lawyer and other defenders may, in accordance with the procedures stipulated in Article 36 of the Criminal Procedure Law, go to the People's Court to consult, extract, and copy the materials concerning the facts of the crime charged in the case, and meet and correspond with the defendant. The defense lawyer may also, in accordance with the provisions of Article 37 of the Criminal Procedure Law, collect materials relevant to the case from witnesses or other relevant units or individuals, apply to the People's Procuratorate or the People's Court to collect or obtain evidence, and apply to the People's Court to notify witnesses to testify in court. With the permission of the People's Procuratorate or the People's Court, and with the consent of the victim or his close relatives, or the witnesses provided by the victim, the defense lawyer may collect materials relevant to the case from them.

During the court trial, if the defense lawyer, when presenting evidence of the defendant's innocence or lesser culpability, considers that evidence materials proving the defendant's innocence or lesser culpability collected by the investigating authority or the People's Procuratorate during the investigation or review for prosecution need to be presented in court, the defense lawyer may apply to the People's Court to obtain such evidence materials from the People's Procuratorate, and may go to the People's Court to consult, extract, and copy such evidence materials.

14. For lawyers who consult, extract, and copy the litigation documents, technical appraisal materials, and the materials concerning the facts of the crime charged in the case, only the necessary production costs for copying the materials may be charged, and no fees under other names shall be charged. The standard for production costs shall be unified nationwide and shall be determined by the Supreme People's Court and the Supreme People's Procuratorate in consultation with the competent state pricing authority.

15. Article 37 of the Criminal Procedure Law stipulates: "With the consent of the witnesses or other relevant units or individuals, a defense lawyer may collect materials relevant to the case from them, or may apply to the People's Procuratorate or the People's Court to collect or obtain evidence, or apply to the People's Court to notify witnesses to testify in court." If a defense lawyer applies to the People's Procuratorate or the People's Court to collect or obtain evidence, and the People's Procuratorate or the People's Court considers that investigation and evidence collection are necessary, the People's Procuratorate or the People's Court shall collect and obtain the evidence themselves, and shall not issue a permission for investigation to the lawyer to allow the lawyer to collect or obtain the evidence.

16. Article 40 of the Criminal Procedure Law stipulates: "The private prosecutor and his legal representative in a private prosecution case, and the party and his legal representative in an incidental civil action, have the right to retain an agent ad litem at any time." In accordance with this provision, the retention of an agent ad litem by a private prosecutor and his legal representative, or by a party to an incidental civil action and his legal representative, shall not be limited to "before the trial begins."

V. Evidence

17. Article 97 of the Criminal Procedure Law stipulates: "Investigators may question witnesses at the witness's place of work or residence," and "when necessary, they may also notify the witness to give testimony at the People's Procuratorate or the public security organ." When investigators question witnesses, they shall do so in accordance with the provisions of Article 97 of the Criminal Procedure Law and may not designate other locations.

18. Paragraph 2 of Article 120 of the Criminal Procedure Law stipulates: "If a medical appraisal of personal injury is disputed and requires a new appraisal, or a medical appraisal of mental illness, it shall be conducted by a hospital designated by the people's government at the provincial level." When the People's Court, during the court trial, finds that the appraisal conclusion made by a hospital designated by the provincial people's government is questionable after cross-examination and cannot be used as the basis for deciding the case, it may separately entrust another hospital designated by the provincial people's government to conduct a supplementary appraisal or a new appraisal. It may not separately entrust other appraisal institutions to conduct a supplementary appraisal or a new appraisal.

19. Article 117 of the Criminal Procedure Law stipulates: "When necessary for investigation of a crime, the People's Procuratorate and the public security authority may, in accordance with regulations, inquire about or freeze the criminal suspect's deposits or remittances." In accordance with this provision, the People's Procuratorate and the public security authority may not deduct or transfer deposits or remittances. If a criminal suspect dies during the investigation or review for prosecution, and the deposits or remittances of the criminal suspect should be confiscated according to law or returned to the victim, they may apply to the People's Court for a ruling to notify the financial institution that froze the deposits or remittances of the criminal suspect to turn them over to the state treasury or return them to the victim.

VI. Release on Guarantee and Residential Surveillance

20. Article 52 of the Criminal Procedure Law stipulates: "A criminal suspect or defendant in custody, his legal representative, or his close relatives have the right to apply for release on guarantee." Article 96 stipulates: "If the criminal suspect is arrested, the retained lawyer may apply for release on guarantee on his behalf." When a criminal suspect or defendant in custody, his legal representative, close relatives, or lawyer applies for release on guarantee, the authority with the power to decide shall reply within seven days as to whether the application is approved. If release on guarantee is approved, the procedures for release on guarantee shall be handled according to law; if release on guarantee is not approved, the applicant shall be informed and the reasons for disapproval explained.

21. Article 53 of the Criminal Procedure Law stipulates: "To grant release on guarantee to a criminal suspect or defendant, the criminal suspect or defendant shall be ordered to provide a guarantor or pay a deposit." In accordance with this provision, a suspect or defendant may not be required to provide both a guarantor and pay a deposit.

22. If a criminal suspect is subject to release on guarantee with a deposit, the amount of the deposit shall be determined by the deciding authority based on the specific circumstances of the case. The deposit for release on guarantee shall be uniformly collected and kept by the public security organs. Whether the guarantor for release on guarantee has fulfilled the guarantee obligations shall be determined by the public security organs, and the decision to fine the guarantor shall also be made by the public security organs. Specific measures shall be formulated by the Ministry of Public Security in conjunction with the Supreme People's Court, the Supreme People's Procuratorate, and the Ministry of State Security.

23. A criminal suspect or defendant subjected to release on guarantee or residential surveillance shall not leave the city, county, or his residence without justifiable reasons. If there are justifiable reasons requiring leaving the city, county, or his residence, approval from the executing authority shall be obtained. If the release on guarantee or residential surveillance was decided by the People's Procuratorate or the People's Court, the executing authority shall obtain the consent of the deciding authority before approving the criminal suspect or defendant to leave the city, county, or his residence.

24. A criminal suspect or defendant under residential surveillance does not need approval to meet with his retained lawyer.

VII. Detention and Arrest

25. The Criminal Procedure Law stipulates that detention shall be executed by the public security organs. For cases directly accepted by the People's Procuratorate, the detention decision made by the People's Procuratorate shall be delivered to the public security organs for execution, and the public security organs shall execute it immediately. The People's Procuratorate may assist the public security organs in the execution.

26. The revised Criminal Procedure Law has amended the previous condition for arrest in the original Criminal Procedure Law that "the principal criminal facts have been found clear" to "there is evidence to prove the existence of criminal facts." The phrase "there is evidence to prove the existence of criminal facts" means that the following circumstances are simultaneously present:

(1) There is evidence to prove that a criminal act has occurred;
(2) There is evidence to prove that the criminal act was committed by the criminal suspect;
(3) The evidence proving that the criminal suspect committed the criminal act has been verified.

The criminal facts may be one of several criminal acts committed by the criminal suspect.

27. When the People's Procuratorate reviews a case submitted by a public security organ for approval of arrest, it shall make a decision to approve or disapprove the arrest, and shall not conduct a separate investigation into the case for which approval of arrest is requested.

28. For a decision by the People's Procuratorate to approve an arrest, the public security organ shall execute it immediately and promptly deliver the execution receipt to the People's Procuratorate that made the approval decision. If the arrest is not executed, the receipt shall also be delivered to the People's Procuratorate, with an explanation of the reasons for non-execution. For a decision by the People's Procuratorate not to approve an arrest, the public security organ shall, upon receiving the decision not to approve the arrest, immediately release the criminal suspect in custody or change the compulsory measures, and shall deliver the execution receipt to the People's Procuratorate that made the disapproval decision within three days of receiving the decision not to approve the arrest.

VIII. Time Periods and Case Handling Time Limits

29. Regarding the calculation of time periods in criminal proceedings, if the last day of a time period falls on a holiday, the day after the holiday shall be considered the expiration date of the time period. However, for the period during which a criminal suspect, defendant, or criminal offender is in custody, it shall end on the day the period expires, and the period in custody shall not be extended to the day after the holiday due to the holiday.

30. When a public security organ requests an extension of the custody period for a case, it shall make the request seven days before the expiration of the custody period, and shall submit in writing the main facts of the case for which the extension of custody is requested and the specific reasons for the extension. The People's Procuratorate shall make a decision before the expiration of the custody period.

31. For cases directly filed and investigated by the Supreme People's Procuratorate, if the conditions stipulated in Articles 124, 126, and 127 of the Criminal Procedure Law are met and an extension of the investigation custody period for the criminal suspect is necessary, the Supreme People's Procuratorate shall decide according to law.

32. In accordance with Article 128 of the Criminal Procedure Law, if during the investigation period, the public security organ discovers that the criminal suspect has committed another significant crime and recalculates the investigation custody period, the public security organ shall decide, and no longer requires approval from the People's Procuratorate. However, it must report to the People's Procuratorate for record, and the People's Procuratorate may exercise supervision.

33. Article 122 of the Criminal Procedure Law stipulates: "The period for conducting a psychiatric appraisal of a criminal suspect shall not be included in the case handling time limit." In accordance with the above provision, in cases where the criminal suspect or defendant is in custody, only the time for the psychiatric appraisal of the criminal suspect or defendant is not included in the case handling time limit; all other appraisal times shall be included in the case handling time limit. For cases where the case handling time limit expires due to a lengthy appraisal time and the case cannot be concluded, from the date of expiration, the compulsory measures against the criminal suspect or defendant in custody shall be changed to release on guarantee or residential surveillance.

IX. Conclusion of Investigation

34. If the People's Procuratorate, upon accepting a case transferred for review for prosecution by a public security organ at the same level, considers that the case should be prosecuted by a higher People's Procuratorate or another People's Procuratorate at the same level in accordance with the jurisdictional provisions of the Criminal Procedure Law, the People's Procuratorate shall transfer the case to the People's Procuratorate with jurisdiction for review for prosecution.

X. Transfer for Prosecution

35. In accordance with Article 150 of the Criminal Procedure Law, when a People's Procuratorate initiates a public prosecution, it shall transfer to the People's Court the indictment, the list of evidence, the list of witnesses, and copies or photographs of the main evidence of all criminal facts. Some specific issues concerning the materials to be transferred shall be handled in the following manner:

(1) The list of witnesses transferred by the People's Procuratorate shall include the names of witnesses who provided testimony before the initiation of the prosecution. The list of witnesses shall set out the witnesses' names, ages, genders, occupations, addresses, and contact information. For witnesses whom the People's Procuratorate does not intend to call to testify, the Procuratorate need not state the reasons for not calling them.

(2) The list of evidence transferred by the People's Procuratorate shall be a list of the evidence materials collected before the initiation of the prosecution.

(3) Issues such as the victim's name, address, contact information, whether there are any properties of the defendant that have been seized or frozen, and their storage location, the type of compulsory measures taken against the defendant, whether the defendant is in custody and the place of custody, etc., shall be set out in the indictment by the People's Procuratorate, and no separate materials need to be transferred. However, if it is inappropriate to state the victim's name, address, or contact information in the indictment due to involving the victim's privacy or protecting the victim's personal safety, such information shall be transferred separately to the People's Court.

(4) If copies of appraisal conclusions and records of inquests and examinations have already been transferred as main evidence, and the names of the appraisers and the persons who made the records of inquests and examinations are already indicated, no separate transfer is necessary.

36. In accordance with Article 150 of the Criminal Procedure Law, when a People's Procuratorate initiates a public prosecution, it shall transfer to the People's Court copies or photographs of the main evidence of all criminal facts. "Main evidence" includes:

(1) The main evidence among the various types of evidence involved in the indictment;
(2) Evidence identified as "main evidence" among multiple pieces of evidence of the same type;
(3) Evidence of statutory sentencing circumstances such as voluntary surrender, meritorious service, recidivism, discontinuation, attempted offense, or legitimate defense.

36. When a people's procuratorate initiates a public prosecution for a specific case, the "main evidence" shall be determined by the people's procuratorate in accordance with the above provisions.

37. Article 150 of the Criminal Procedure Law provides: "After a people's court has reviewed a case in which a public prosecution has been initiated, if the indictment contains clear facts of the crime and is accompanied by a list of evidence, a list of witnesses, and copies or photographs of the main evidence, it shall decide to hold a court session for trial." A people's court shall accept all cases in which a people's procuratorate has initiated a public prosecution. After a people's court has reviewed a case in which a public prosecution has been initiated, if the indictment contains clear facts of the crime and is accompanied by a list of evidence, a list of witnesses, and copies or photographs of the main evidence, it shall decide to hold a court session for trial and may not refuse to hold a court session on the ground that the above materials are insufficient. If the materials submitted by the people's procuratorate are lacking the above materials, the people's court may notify the people's procuratorate to supplement the materials, and the people's procuratorate shall provide the supplement within three days from the date of receipt of the notice.

The time for a people's court to review a case in which a public prosecution has been initiated shall be included in the trial period of the people's court.

38. For public prosecution cases subject to summary procedure, regardless of whether the people's procuratorate sends personnel to appear in court, it shall transfer all case files and evidence materials to the people's court.

11. Trial in Court

39. Article 154 of the Criminal Procedure Law provides that when a court session opens, the presiding judge shall ascertain whether the parties are present. In accordance with the above provision, the presiding judge shall ascertain whether the parties are present, and it cannot be provided that the court clerk shall do so.

40. Regarding the order of questioning witnesses in court trials, the court trial shall be conducted under the direction of the presiding judge, and the order of questioning of witnesses by the public prosecutor and the defense counsel shall be determined by the presiding judge.

41. Article 158, paragraph 1 of the Criminal Procedure Law provides: "During the course of a court trial, if the collegial panel has doubts about the evidence, it may announce an adjournment to investigate and verify the evidence." Article 159, paragraph 1 provides: "During the course of a court trial, the parties, the defense counsel, and the agents ad litem have the right to request the court to notify new witnesses to appear, to obtain new physical evidence, and to request a new expert evaluation or inspection." In accordance with the above provisions, a people's court may request from a people's procuratorate evidence materials that need investigation and verification; a people's court may also, upon application by the defense counsel or the defendant, request from a people's procuratorate evidence materials collected during the investigation and examination and prosecution concerning the defendant's innocence or lesser guilt. The people's procuratorate shall transfer such materials within three days from the date of receipt of the people's court's decision requesting the transfer of evidence materials.

42. Evidence materials presented, read out, or played in court by a people's procuratorate shall be transferred to the people's court at the court session; if it is truly impossible to transfer them at the court session, they shall be transferred within three days after the adjournment. For testimony of a witness who did not appear in court that is presented, read out, or played in court, if the witness has provided different testimony, the people's procuratorate shall transfer all the witness's testimony within three days after the adjournment.

43. Article 169 of the amended Criminal Procedure Law provides: "If a people's procuratorate discovers that a people's court's trial of a case violates the litigation procedures provided by law, it has the right to propose corrective opinions to the people's court." Where a people's procuratorate proposes corrective opinions regarding a court trial activity that violates legal procedures, it shall propose such opinions after the court trial.

12. Second Instance

44. Article 188 of the Criminal Procedure Law provides: "For cases in which the people's procuratorate has filed a protest or public prosecution cases tried by a second instance people's court, the people's procuratorate at the corresponding level shall send personnel to appear in court." In accordance with this provision, the personnel appearing in court in the second instance trial shall be the procuratorial personnel of the people's procuratorate at the corresponding level.

45. For cases in which the people's procuratorate has filed a protest or public prosecution cases tried by a second instance people's court, if the procuratorial personnel and defense counsel appearing in court in the second instance need to present, read out, or play evidence that has already been transferred to the people's court in the first instance, the procuratorial personnel and defense counsel appearing in court may request the court to present, read out, or play such evidence.

46. For cases in which the people's procuratorate has filed a protest, after review by the second instance people's court, if it is considered that the defendant should be sentenced to death, it shall be handled in accordance with the provisions of Article 189 of the Criminal Procedure Law. That is, if the second instance people's court considers that the facts found in the original judgment are not erroneous but the application of the law is erroneous or the sentence is improper, it shall amend the judgment; if it considers that the facts in the original judgment are unclear or the evidence is insufficient, it may amend the judgment after ascertaining the facts or remand the case for retrial. Where the second instance people's court directly amends the judgment to a death sentence, regardless of whether the power to review the death sentence has been delegated, it shall report to the Supreme People's Court for approval.

13. Death Penalty Review

47. When a high people's court reviews a case in which a death sentence has been imposed with a two-year suspension of execution, it shall render a decision either to approve or not to approve, and may not increase the defendant's punishment.

14. Illegal Gains and Property

48. As for illegal gains and property, except for property that is returned to the victim in accordance with the law and contraband that is destroyed in accordance with the law, all must be turned over to the State Treasury. No unit or individual may misappropriate or dispose of them without authorization. The handling of illegal gains and property shall be carried out in accordance with the provisions of Article 198 of the Criminal Procedure Law, and shall be handled according to different circumstances as follows:

(1) Physical objects used as evidence shall be transferred together with the case file in accordance with the law. If transfer is not appropriate, their inventory, photographs, or other certifying documents shall be transferred together with the case file, and the case may not be refused to be accepted on the ground that the illegal gains and property have not been transferred.

(2) For illegal gains frozen by an investigation authority in a financial institution, the financial institution's certifying documents shall be transferred together with the case file to the people's court. After the people's court renders a final judgment, it shall notify the financial institution to turn over the funds to the State Treasury, and the financial institution shall deliver a receipt of execution to the people's court.

(3) For sealed and seized illegal gains and property that, in accordance with the law, are not to be transferred, evidence inventories, photographs, or other certifying documents shall be transferred together with the case file. After the people's court renders a final judgment, it shall notify the authority that carried out the sealing and seizure to turn over the property to the State Treasury, and that authority shall deliver a receipt of execution to the people's court.

When state security authorities handle criminal cases that endanger state security in accordance with the law, the provisions of these Regulations concerning public security authorities shall apply. These Regulations shall come into effect on the date of their promulgation. If any interpretations or provisions regarding the implementation of the Criminal Procedure Law formulated by the Supreme People's Court, the Supreme People's Procuratorate, the Ministry of Public Security, or the Ministry of State Security are inconsistent with these Regulations, these Regulations shall prevail.

January 19, 1998
